claims.text: Joan of Arc, a peasant girl in her teens, helped French forces lift the English siege of Orléans in 1429.
Eleanor of Aquitaine lived in the 1100s, Catherine de' Medici in the 1500s and Marie Antoinette in the 1700s, so none took part in the 1429 siege.
Joan of Arc was about 17 at the siege of Orléans.
Joan was captured in 1430 and executed in 1431 after a church trial held under English control.
A retrial in 1456 cleared Joan, and she was canonized in 1920.
